name: Mehmed II Reorganizes the Ottoman State
summary: Following Constantinople's conquest, Mehmed II undertakes comprehensive state reorganization: the Palace School trains the elite devshirme administrators who run the empire; the Grand Vizier (replacing the earlier system of royal family administration) coordinates government; the Kanunname codifies administrative and criminal law; Mehmed populates the capital by requiring resettlement from conquered peoples.

_quarry.structural_significance: Mehmed's post-conquest reorganization creates the Ottoman administrative system that survives into the 19th century; the devshirme meritocracy, talented men of slave origin rising to be Grand Viziers, is the Ottoman solution to the problem of noble hereditary power blocking royal authority; the system produces extraordinary administrators but also creates a state where the sultan's personal rule is mediated entirely through slaves, removing traditional checks on royal tyranny
